applicable_when: The kernel is a simple pointwise bias-add + ReLU over 191M float32 elements. With XBLOCK=128, each CTA covers 128 elements = 512 bytes = 4 cache lines. Without vectorization hints, the Triton compiler emits 32-bit scalar loads (LDG.32) rather than 128-bit vectorized loads (LDG.128). This causes 4x more L1TEX transactions per warp, each incurring a full round-trip latency, explaining why 83.7% of scheduler cycles are spent waiting on L1TEX. Increasing XBLOCK to 1024 reduces grid size by 8x (from 1.49M to 186K CTAs), amortizes launch overhead, and gives each warp more independent loads to hide latency. Adding tl.max_contiguous and tl.multiple_of hints tells the compiler the access is contiguous and aligned, enabling LDG.128 (float4) vectorized loads — 4 floats per transaction instead of 1.
